summary.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready.” It is the standardized simplified form of 備, whose older graph is interpreted as a person with an arrow container, an image associated with readiness.

formation.text: 備 is interpreted as 人, a person, together with 𤰈, an image of arrows in a container. Read as a person carrying the container, the scene suggests being prepared. A separate analysis treats the whole graph as a picture of a quiver, while the traditional lexicographic account assigns 𤰈 a sound role; the sound comparison cannot be independently checked. These interpretations do not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 备 is the standardized simplified form of 備.

components.text: In the carrying-scene interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the arrow container. Another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, or a quiver. The received analysis also assigns it a sound role, but the component’s historical reading has not been independently recovered.

sound_limitation.text: The proposed sound role cannot be checked against a verified historical reading for 𤰈. 備 has a Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, but it does not independently establish the component’s identity, reading, or sound relation to the host.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories. The available descriptions do not establish the earliest appearance or a sequence among these forms.

The modern printed right-hand form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Some bronze forms change the lower part of 𤰈 to 用, tentatively interpreted as a sound element; these accounts do not establish a dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme standardized 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but its proposed role as the direct source of 备 is not established.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with readiness, but does not show that this was the word’s earliest meaning. 備 is also reported as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” in a bronze inscription. This is understood as a whole-graph sound-based borrowing, but the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are unrecovered, so the proposed sound match cannot be verified.

Reported uses include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or a continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the association with preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.

overview.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready” and is the simplified form of 備. One interpretation of 備 shows a person carrying an arrow container, a picture associated with readiness; it does not prove the word’s earliest meaning.

components.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 is the person carrying the arrow container.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container; its proposed sound role lacks an independently verified historical reading.

relationships.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person in a carrying scene.
𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container in the proposed carrying scene; another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.

A historical lexicographic analysis and another interpretation assign 𤰈 a sound role in 備. No independent historical pronunciation for 𤰈 was recovered, so the proposed relation cannot be checked through a verified component–host sound comparison.
The 1956 scheme lists 备 as the simplified form corresponding to 備.
俻 is documented as a variant of 備; this does not establish that 备 specifically derives from 俻.
